text: Follow the day’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The South Australian premier, Peter Malinauskas , says there is optimism that steel making will continue in his state, after the closure of a major blast furnace at Whyalla was announced yesterday. Speaking to ABC News Breakfast from Whyalla and donned in some hi-vis, Malinauskas says there was disappointment, heartbreak, but also a sense of inevitability when the announcement was made. [Whyalla] has the capacity to be a viable operation but it hasn’t been recapitalised. The blast furnace is over 60 years old. It was first built in 1965 and blast furnaces of this age not to be realigned on a frequent basis. This hasn’t been done in 20 years. The fact it’s still going is a miracle. We need to have the plant recapitalised and that’s exactly the plan we have in conjunction with the federal government … if we lose this capacity behind me, this country doesn’t have structural steel-making capacity and we can’t afford that. title: US supreme court blocks Trump administration from changing mail ballot rules for midterm elections – live
text: 20.01 EDT US supreme court blocks Trump administration from changing mail ballot rules for midterm elections The US supreme court on Monday denied a request from the Trump administration to implement new US Postal Service restrictions on mail voting in the 2026 midterm elections, which have already started. The decision allows states to continue sending out mail ballots without meeting new requirements the USPS tried to impose to comply with an executive order from Donald Trump, who insists without evidence that vote-by-mail is riddled with fraud. The application for the high court to lift a lower court order blocking the implementation of the new postal service rule was denied by the court with just two noted dissents, from the conservative justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas . “The Government is unlikely to succeed on the merits of its challenge to the District Court’s preliminary injunction,” the brief, unsigned ruling stated. “And the equitable factors applicable for obtaining emergency relief from this Court do not favor a stay.” In his eight-page dissent, Alito argued the opposite, writing: “The Government is likely to succeed on the merits of its appeal.” Justice Brett

title: Supreme court rejects Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections
text: A mail-in ballot during the Pennsylvania primary election in Philadelphia on 19 May 2026. Photograph: Hannah Beier/Reuters View image in fullscreen A mail-in ballot during the Pennsylvania primary election in Philadelphia on 19 May 2026. Photograph: Hannah Beier/Reuters US supreme court Supreme court rejects Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections Decision allows states to send ballots under process followed for years even as president tried to limit system Associated Press Mon 14 Sep 2026 20.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The supreme court on Monday rejected Donald Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for now, capping a flurry of last-minute legal action with voting in the midterm elections already underway. The decision allows states to continue sending out mail ballots under the same processes they have used for years. The Trump administration had asked the court, once again at the center of a roiling political controversy, to clear the way for restrictions before the pivotal November contests for control of Congress.
